lines: I start the repo on December 14 as a prediction-market arbitrage bot built from a Claude skill. A week later it moves to fifteen-minute crypto markets. 15 commits.
The scripts become a web service with auth, markets and bot endpoints.
Two days of hardening: ten security and correctness fixes, a paper-trading core, retries and rate limits (PR 7). 18 commits.
One day of "waves": VPIN, Monte Carlo Kelly, lifecycle tracking, an operator dashboard, alerts, CI/CD.
A "quick wins" commit strips 226 lines of safety code, and the test run halts on drift. 120 commits.
March 8: 898 paper trades turn out to be fake (no fees, instant fills). I rebuild the paper trader that evening to check its fills against real trades.
March 28: live code that does not match its backtest (a tenfold scaling slip) leads to a five-step launch rule: backtest, matching check, a day in shadow, review, smallest size.
I install a code-review graph, and "query the graph before editing" becomes a rule. 174 commits.
April 7: a backtest turns out to have used data before it was public, and I kill the strategy.
The /check skill runs only the tests a change touches. 74 commits.
Two broken upstream releases in one week break the build, and both are fenced off. Rate limiting is made spoof-resistant. 46 commits, 15 merged pull requests.
The knowledge graph becomes the agents' default way around the code. 39 commits.
July 13: I switch off the live bot. I generalize six guardrail skills from the bot's own skills.
August 20: I split the data into raw, cleaned and analysis layers, with a rule that a headline number cites its table. The first table disagrees with a number already shipped.
August 26: I publish the guardrails as a public repo.
Candidate ideas get a review by a second model before any data is pulled. One agent builds, another checks.
September 22: memecoin graduation trades close with no edge.

A knowledge system: a verdict registry that renders the status page, a citation checker that fails the test suite, the whole record re-checked by a separate reviewer agent. 572 commits (380 by a second coding agent).
A research-protocol skill, a shared statistics library and a data-completeness policy, each built by one agent and reviewed by another. The dead-code merge removes 2,598 lines.
October 17: I freeze the audit's plan. October 25: the checker passes it on the third run.
